name: PawStyle by Lola — Independent Streams (no cross-talk)
description: Frontend and backend work independently to build Lola's boutique dog apparel shop. No steering events. Tests pure parallel throughput + quality in isolation. Inspired by @_justlolathings.

turns.content:
Build the PawStyle by Lola product listing page — a boutique dog apparel shop inspired by Lola (@_justlolathings), the most fashionable pup on Instagram.

Requirements:
- Single HTML file with embedded CSS/JS
- Flexbox grid, 3 columns, responsive (1 col on mobile)
- Header: "PawStyle by Lola" with tagline "Where every pup is a fashionista"
- Purple gradient header (#7c3aed to #6d28d9)
- 6 products on lavender (#e9d5ff) cards:
  1. Lola's Signature Bandana - $12.00 (show a "Lola's Pick" badge)
  2. Cozy Knit Sweater - $35.00
  3. Rainy Day Raincoat - $45.00
  4. Adventure Booties (4-pack) - $28.00
  5. Dapper Bow Tie - $15.00 (show a "Lola's Pick" badge)
  6. Walk-in-Style Harness - $40.00
- Each card: name, price, gray placeholder image 300x200, box-shadow 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)
- Size selector per card: XS (Chihuahua), S (Pom), M (Beagle), L (Lab), XL (Golden)
- Purple (#7c3aed) 'Add to Cart' button, white text, rounded corners
- Footer with link to Lola's Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/_justlolathings/
- Fetch from GET http://localhost:8080/api/products on load, fallback to hardcoded

Use write_file for each file.

File written. Lola's shop is looking great! Now add a slide-in Cart sidebar from the right. Shows item name, selected size (with breed label, e.g. 'M (Beagle)'), price, quantity +/- buttons, line totals, and a grand total. Cart persists in localStorage. Use write_file to update.

Done. Final step: add a checkout flow. When user clicks 'Checkout' in cart, POST cart contents to http://localhost:8080/api/orders as JSON. Show a confirmation modal with order number (random 6-digit) and a paw-print icon. Include the message 'Lola approves your style!' in the confirmation. Handle API errors gracefully with a retry button. Use write_file.

Build the PawStyle by Lola REST API using Python stdlib http.server — the backend for Lola's boutique dog apparel shop.

Endpoints:
- GET /api/products — JSON array of 6 products with id, name, price, sizes, image, and lola_pick boolean:
  1. Lola's Signature Bandana $12.00 (lola_pick: true)
  2. Cozy Knit Sweater $35.00
  3. Rainy Day Raincoat $45.00
  4. Adventure Booties (4-pack) $28.00
  5. Dapper Bow Tie $15.00 (lola_pick: true)
  6. Walk-in-Style Harness $40.00
  Sizes: ["XS","S","M","L","XL"]
- GET /api/products/<id> — single product, 404 if not found
- CORS headers on all responses
- Port 8080

Use write_file.

Written. Now add POST /api/orders endpoint for Lola's checkout. Accepts JSON body {"items": [{"product_id": 1, "size": "M", "quantity": 2}]}. Validate product IDs exist (1-6), sizes are valid (XS/S/M/L/XL), quantities > 0. Return {"order_id": "<random 6 digits>", "total": <calculated total>, "items_count": <n>, "message": "Lola approves your style!"}. Return 400 with error message for invalid input. Use write_file.

Done. Final step: add GET /api/health returning {"status": "ok", "store": "PawStyle by Lola", "uptime": <seconds since start>, "orders_count": <total orders placed>, "products_count": 6}. Also add request logging — print each request method, path, status code, and response time in ms to stdout. Use write_file.
